_comment: Loan-success-score component weights, per position. Unlike data/score_weights.json (permanent transfers), there's no value_for_money or resale_profit component: most loans carry no real fee (the packaged fee is 0 even when a real loan fee was agreed - see fetch_transfer_types.py), and a loan doesn't end in a sale of its own. playing_time is weighted heavily across every position - whether the loan actually delivered game time is usually the central question a loan gets judged on, independent of how well the player performed when they did play. value_growth and rating are both deliberately FLAT across every position (0.12/0.20), same reasoning as data/score_weights.json: value_growth is a single global percentile rank with no position grouping, so there's no football-role reason for its weight to vary by position; rating is the same metric (FotMob's overall per-match quality score) regardless of role, unlike attacking/defensive/possession which are literally different stats by position - and it reflects more than any one counting stat can (positioning, decision-making, composure), so it's now weighted like a real component (0.20) rather than a token one. rating's move up (2-9% originally, to a flat 0.10, then to a flat 0.20) is funded from perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time (scaled down proportionally) rather than from value_growth (already flat) or attacking/defensive/possession (kept as tuned). Goalkeeper's playing_time is the one exception to that funding rule: it used to sit at 0.45 (deliberately the highest of any position/loan combination - a club fields exactly one starting keeper, and a loan spell's whole point is usually the game time itself, so both reasons for weighting playing_time heavily stack for a loan goalkeeper specifically), but the two rating bumps drained it to 0.34 since perf_level/perf_delta are already 0 for goalkeepers and had nothing else to give. Restored to 0.44 here, funded from defensive (0.29 -> 0.22) and possession (0.05 -> 0.02) instead, so that reasoning isn't silently lost again. Each FotMob component is only known for the loans FotMob has tenure stats for (scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py, same fetch as permanent transfers) - its weight is dropped and the rest renormalized for a loan missing it, same pattern as data/score_weights.json. Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row must sum to 1.0. rating was raised from a flat 0.20 to 0.30 for the four outfield defensive sub-positions (Defensive Midfield, Centre-Back, Left-Back, Right-Back) and the broad Defender fallback, funded entirely from defensive (0.17/0.24/0.22/0.22/0.15 down to 0.07/0.14/0.12/0.12/0.05) - same fix as data/score_weights.json, checked directly against the loan dataset first: rating correlates with loan_success_score more strongly than the defensive bucket for every one of these positions (0.67-0.77 vs. 0.29-0.52, sample sizes smaller than the permanent-transfer table since loan FotMob coverage is thinner), the same underweighted-top-predictor pattern, so the same fix was applied. Central/Attacking/Left/Right Midfield were checked too and did NOT show this pattern (rating's correlation edge over attacking was small and rating already carried more weight than attacking there), so those rows were left unchanged, mirroring the permanent-transfer table's finding.
_sub_positions_comment: Sub-position weight overrides, same idea and same rows as data/score_weights.json's _sub_positions (see that file's comment for the full rationale) - a player's actual career-wide fielded sub-position selects one of these rows instead of the broad position row above when one exists; percentile ranking still groups by the broad position. value_growth and rating are flat 0.12/0.20 here too, same as the broad rows above and for the same reason - neither has a football-role basis to vary at this level either. Full-back's defensive is raised to 0.22 (funded from perf_level/perf_delta/attacking, same as the permanent-transfer table) - capped below Centre-Back's 0.24 rather than matching the permanent table's 0.26 exactly, since a full-back shouldn't out-weight a centre-back on defending.
